Currently responsible for managing the temple affairs, Ms. Ying (a pseudonym), a descendant of the Chow family, revealed to a photojournalist that years ago her grandfather, a Tanka fisherman, unexpectedly retrieved a wooden carving of "Four Sisters" while out at sea. Her grandfather brought the carving home and gave it to young Ying as a toy, and she even sewed clothes for the statue. Unexpectedly, Ying soon fell ill with a high fever, and her grandmother received a dream visitation from "Seven Sisters", who instructed her grandfather to enshrine and worship the statue at a temple. The Chow family then obeyed the divine instruction and built today's Seven Sisters Temple.

The Fairy Sister Temple is renowned for its efficacy in seeking romantic matches. Ms. Ying further shared a romantic anecdote. On the evening of the sixth day of the seventh lunar month three years ago, a slightly chubby young man with a bit of "baby fat" waited patiently in front of the temple until midnight of the seventh day of the seventh lunar month to pay his respects, and returned to do the same the following year. Just yesterday evening on the sixth, the young man, dressed in red, arrived hand-in-hand with his girlfriend to fulfil his vow. Ms. Ying did not initially recognise him, until he awkwardly smiled at her while holding his girlfriend's hand, at which point Ying finally recognised the devoted young man, witnessing how his sincere love had blossomed into a happy result.

When discussing the insights for worshipping at the Seven Sisters Temple, Ms. Ying believes it is essentially about communicating with the deities: "Just say whatever is on your mind, pour out your troubles to Seven Sisters." Like having a chat, if one wishes to know Seven Sisters' advice and outcome, one can cast the divination blocks (bei). During the Qixi Festival, the Fairy Sister Temple is not only a sacred place for seeking blessed romantic matches, but also a harbour of refuge for devotees to pour out their hearts.
